transcription.notes: One top-level problem (I. Satellite’s orbit transfer) with printed parts a)–g), points 1+2+1+1+1+3+1 = 10; no paper total is printed. The official solution labels the sketch for part g) as „h) (1 point)“; it is kept verbatim at the end of the solution and belongs to part g). In the solution of f) the printed first equation has the term $\frac{C/m}{r^3}$ and $C/m = GMR_1$ (dimensionally $(C/m)^2$ would be expected); kept verbatim. In the solution of e) the printed intermediate step has $\sqrt{2}R_0$ under the root (the final line uses $2R_0$); kept verbatim. The comma after $R_1$ in the statement of f) is printed in bold. The text layer loses the math layout (Word/Equation export) and was used only as a spelling cross-check.

problems.title: Satellite’s orbit transfer
problems.statement: In the near future we ourselves may take part in launching of a satellite which, in point of view of physics, requires only the use of simple mechanics.

figures.alt: A small circular orbit of radius R0 around the Earth M, with the satellite m moving on it and the velocity u0 drawn tangent to it. An elliptical transfer orbit touches the circle at point Q, where the velocity u1 is drawn, and reaches the far point P, where the velocity u2 is drawn perpendicular to the dotted line of length R1 from M to P.

Axes X and Y with the Earth M at the origin; a dotted circle labelled with an arrow “mean orbit of radius R1”; the satellite m at distance r from M, at angle θ from the X axis, on a solid perturbed trajectory that crosses the dotted circle.

parts.label: a)
parts.statement: A satellite of mass $m$ is presently circling the Earth of mass $M$ in a circular orbit of radius $R_0$. What is the speed $(u_0)$ of mass $m$ in terms of $M, R_0$ and the universal gravitation constant $G$?

parts.label: b)
parts.statement: We are to put this satellite into a trajectory that will take it to point P at distance $R_1$ from the centre of the Earth by increasing (almost instantaneously) its velocity at point Q from $u_0$ to $u_1$. What is the value of $u_1$ in terms of $u_0, R_0, R_1$?

parts.label: c)
parts.statement: Deduce the minimum value of $u_1$ in term of $u_0$ that will allow the satellite to leave the Earth’s influence completely.

parts.label: d)
parts.statement: (Referring to part b.) What is the velocity $(u_2)$ of the satellite at point P in terms of $u_0, R_0, R_1$?

parts.label: e)
parts.statement:
Now, we want to change the orbit of the satellite at point P into a circular orbit of radius $R_1$ by raising the value of $u_2$ (almost instantaneously) to $u_3$.

What is the magnitude of $u_3$ in terms of $u_2, R_0, R_1$?

parts.label: f)
parts.statement:
If the satellite is slightly and instantaneously perturbed in the radial direction so that it deviates from its previously perfectly circular orbit of radius $R_1$**,** derive the period of its oscillation $T$ of $r$ about the mean distance $R_1$.

**Hint**: Students may make use (if necessary) of the equation of motion of a satellite in orbit:

$$m\left[\frac{d^2}{dt^2}r - \left(\frac{d}{dt}\theta\right)^2 r\right] = -G\frac{Mm}{r^2} \qquad \ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots\ (1)$$

and the conservation of angular momentum:

$$mr^2\frac{d}{dt}\theta = \text{constant} \qquad \ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots\ (2)$$

parts.label: g)
parts.statement: Give a rough sketch of the whole perturbed orbit together with the unperturbed one.

solution.statement:
a) $$\frac{mu_0^{\,2}}{R_0} = \frac{GMm}{R_0^{\,2}}, \qquad u_0 = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R_0}}$$ (1 point)

b) conservation of angular momentum: $mu_1R_0 = mu_2R_1$

conservation of energy: $\tfrac{1}{2}mu_2^{\,2} - \dfrac{GMm}{R_1} = \tfrac{1}{2}mu_1^{\,2} - \dfrac{GMm}{R_0}$

$$\left[\left(\frac{R_0}{R_1}\right)^2 - 1\right]u_1^{\,2} = 2GM\left[\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_0}\right]$$

$$\frac{(R_0 - R_1)(R_0 + R_1)}{R_1^{\,2}}u_1^{\,2} = (2GM)\frac{(R_0 - R_1)}{R_0R_1}$$

$$u_1 = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R_0}}\sqrt{\frac{2R_1}{R_1 + R_0}} = u_0\sqrt{\frac{2R_1}{R_1 + R_0}}$$ (2 points)

c) $$\lim_{R_1 \to \infty} u_1 = \sqrt{2}\,u_0$$ (1 point)

d) $$u_2 = u_1\frac{R_0}{R_1} = u_0\frac{\sqrt{2}\,R_0}{\sqrt{R_1(R_1 + R_0)}}$$ (1 point)

e) $$u_3 = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R_1}} = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R_0}}\sqrt{\frac{R_0}{R_1}} = u_0\sqrt{\frac{R_0}{R_1}}$$

$$= \sqrt{\frac{R_0}{R_1}}\sqrt{\frac{R_1(R_1 + R_0)}{\sqrt{2}R_0}}\,u_2$$

$$u_3 = u_2\sqrt{\frac{R_1 + R_0}{2R_0}}$$ (1 point)

f) (3 points) combining equations (1) and (2) :

$$\frac{d^2}{dt^2}r - \frac{C/m}{r^3} = -\frac{GM}{r^2}$$

and for the circular orbit of radius $R_1$ we have $\dfrac{C}{m} = GMR_1$

hence $$\frac{d^2}{dt^2}r - \frac{GMR_1}{r^3} = -\frac{GM}{r^2}$$

putting $r = R_1 + \eta$, where $\eta \ll R_1$

$$\therefore\ \frac{d^2}{dt^2}\eta - \frac{GMR_1}{R_1^{\,3}\left(1 + \frac{\eta}{R_1}\right)^3} = -\frac{GM}{R_1^{\,2}\left(1 + \frac{\eta}{R_1}\right)^2}$$

$$\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\eta - \frac{GM}{R_1^{\,2}}\left(1 - 3\frac{\eta}{R_1}\right) \approx -\frac{GM}{R_1^{\,2}}\left(1 - 2\frac{\eta}{R_1}\right)$$

$$\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\eta \approx -\frac{GM}{R_1^{\,3}}\eta$$

the frequency of oscillation about mean distance is $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R_1^{\,3}}}$

the period $T = \dfrac{1}{f} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R_1^{\,3}}{GM}}$

Note that this period is the same as the orbital period

h) (1 point)
